hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, for example astrocytes, APOE4 causes impaired ARF6-related recycling of receptors between the cell surface and the endosome, compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Surface biotinylation followed by ELISA showed a significantly lower APOER2 surface-to-total ratio in APOE4 versus APOE3 primary mouse neuronal cultures (53% reduction; n = 3 cohorts, each pooling neurons from at least two mice).
rows.Finding quote: The results obtained show that the ratio of the externally oriented receptors to the total, was significantly lower in APOE4 neurons of APOER2 (Fig. 4A, 53% reduction, p < 0.05) and LRP1 (Fig. 4B, 48.03% reduction, p < 0.05) than those of the corresponding APOE3 cells.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower APOER2 surface-to-total ratio in primary mouse neurons)
rows.Experimental system: Primary neuron-enriched brain cultures from 1–3-day-old APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mouse pups on an α-syn-/- background; each culture pooled 2–3 pups, with FUDR treatment on culture day 3 to inhibit glial proliferation; experiments on culture day 21. Surface proteins were biotinylated for 30 minutes at 4°C, isolated with NeutrAvidin, and quantified alongside total lysates by APOER2 ELISA; ratios were normalized to APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Surface biotinylation followed by ELISA showed a significantly lower LRP1 surface-to-total ratio in APOE4 versus APOE3 primary mouse neuronal cultures (48.03% reduction; three independent cohorts, each pooling neurons from at least two mice).
rows.Finding quote: The results obtained show that the ratio of the externally oriented receptors to the total, was significantly lower in APOE4 neurons of APOER2 (Fig. 4A, 53% reduction, p < 0.05) and LRP1 (Fig. 4B, 48.03% reduction, p < 0.05) than those of the corresponding APOE3 cells.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower LRP1 surface-to-total ratio in primary mouse neurons)
rows.Experimental system: Neuron-enriched primary brain cultures from 1–3-day-old APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mouse pups on an α-syn-/- background; cultures pooled 2–3 pups, received FUDR on day 3 to inhibit glial proliferation, and were assayed on day 21 using cell surface biotinylation and ELISA of surface and total LRP1.

rows.Finding description: Surface biotinylation and ELISA in primary mouse neuronal cultures from three independent cohorts showed no significant difference in the IR surface-to-total ratio between APOE4 and APOE3, despite a 28.77% lower ratio in APOE4 (p = 0.07).
rows.Finding quote: Similar, though less prominent, pattern was evident in IR (Fig. 4 C, 28.77% reduction, p = 0.07), and VEGFR (Fig. 4D, 9.90% reduction, p = 0.15).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in IR surface-to-total ratio in primary mouse neurons)
rows.Experimental system: Primary brain-derived, neuron-enriched cultures from 1–3-day-old APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mouse pups on an α-syn-/- background; each culture pooled 2–3 pups, with experiments performed on culture day 21. Surface proteins were biotinylated, isolated, and quantified alongside total lysates by IR-specific ELISA to calculate the surface-to-total ratio. Three independent cohorts were analyzed after normalization to APOE3. ARF6 involvement and recycling kinetics were not measured.

rows.Finding description: Surface biotinylation and ELISA in three independent primary mouse neuronal culture cohorts showed a reported 9.90% lower VEGFR surface-to-total ratio in APOE4 versus APOE3 cultures, with no significant difference (p = 0.15).
rows.Finding quote: Similar, though less prominent, pattern was evident in IR (Fig. 4 C, 28.77% reduction, p = 0.07), and VEGFR (Fig. 4D, 9.90% reduction, p = 0.15).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in VEGFR surface-to-total ratio in primary mouse neurons)
rows.Experimental system: Primary neuron-enriched brain cultures from 1–3-day-old human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mouse pups on an α-syn-/- background; each culture pooled 2–3 pups. Cultures received FUDR on day 3 to inhibit glial proliferation and were assayed on day 21. Surface proteins were biotinylated for 30 minutes at 4°C, isolated with NeutrAvidin, and VEGFR2 in surface fractions and total lysates was measured by ELISA to calculate the surface-to-total ratio.

rows.Finding description: Double-label confocal microscopy comparing APOE4 with APOE3 primary mouse neurons showed increased APOER2 colocalization with early endosomes (p < 0.05), decreased colocalization with lysosomes (35.89% decrease, p < 0.0001), and no significant difference in colocalization with late endosomes (p = 0.156) or recycling endosomes (p = 0.5154), with 25–37 cells from 2–3 preparations for each receptor–compartment comparison.
rows.Finding quote: Additionally, there was also a decrease in the colocalization of the receptors with the lysosomes in APOE4 neurons that was significant in APOER2 and VEGFR but not in the IR (APOER2 : 35.89% decrease, p < 0.0001; VEGFR: 31.30% decrease, p < 0.05), and in the recycling endosomes in all three receptors (APOER2 : 11.16% decrease, p = 0.5154; IR: 30.88% decrease, p < 0.05; VEGFR: 29.02% decrease, p < 0.05) when compared to APOE3 neurons.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (increased APOER2 colocalization with early endosomes; decreased colocalization with lysosomes; no change in colocalization with late or recycling endosomes)
rows.Experimental system: Primary brain-derived neuronal-enriched cultures from 1–3-day-old APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mouse pups on an alpha-synuclein-null background; 2–3 pups pooled per preparation, FUDR treatment on culture day 3 to inhibit glial proliferation, and experiments on day 21; APOER2 double immunostaining with Rab5, Rab7, CatD, or Rab11, followed by confocal microscopy and M1 colocalization analysis of morphologically selected neurons.

rows.Finding description: Double immunostaining and confocal colocalization analysis of primary mouse neurons showed increased insulin receptor (IR) colocalization with early endosomes, decreased colocalization with late and recycling endosomes (30.88% decrease for recycling endosomes), and no significant difference in lysosomal colocalization in APOE4 versus APOE3 neurons, with 25–37 cells analyzed per receptor–compartment comparison from 2–3 preparations.
rows.Finding quote: Additionally, there was also a decrease in the colocalization of the receptors with the lysosomes in APOE4 neurons that was significant in APOER2 and VEGFR but not in the IR (APOER2 : 35.89% decrease, p < 0.0001; VEGFR: 31.30% decrease, p < 0.05), and in the recycling endosomes in all three receptors (APOER2 : 11.16% decrease, p = 0.5154; IR: 30.88% decrease, p < 0.05; VEGFR: 29.02% decrease, p < 0.05) when compared to APOE3 neurons.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (increased IR colocalization with early endosomes; decreased IR colocalization with late and recycling endosomes; no change in IR colocalization with lysosomes)
rows.Experimental system: Primary brain-derived neurons from 1–3-day-old APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mouse pups on an α-syn-/- background; neuronal-enriched cultures prepared from 2–3 pooled pups, treated with FUDR on culture day 3, and assayed on day 21 without an additional experimental treatment; double immunofluorescent staining for IR and Rab5, Rab7, Rab11, or CatD, followed by confocal microscopy and M1 colocalization analysis of morphologically selected neurons.

rows.Finding description: LRP1 knockdown reduced early-endosome colocalization of APOER2 (38.8%), IR (48.9%), and VEGFR (64.1%; 23–27 neurons from three preparations) in APOE4 primary mouse neurons, abolishing their excess accumulation, and also reduced VEGFR colocalization in APOE3 neurons by 21.6%.
rows.Finding quote: As can be seen, the downregulation of LRP1 had no significant effects on the total levels of the receptors, had no effect on the size of early endosomes (not shown), but did abolish the excess colocalization of these receptors with early endosomes in APOE4 neurons (the percent of reduction when compared to APOE4 control equals to 38.8% in APOER2, 48.9% in IR, and 64.1% in VEGFR). Whereas in APOE3 neurons, the knock-down of LRP1 resulted only in a small, but significant downregulation of the colocalization of VEGFR with the early endosomes (21.6% reduction), but it had no effect on the colocalization of IR.
rows.Finding summary: (LRP1 knockdown in APOE4 neurons) -> (lower early-endosome colocalization of APOER2, IR, and VEGFR; abolished excess accumulation); (LRP1 knockdown in APOE3 neurons) -> (lower early-endosome colocalization of VEGFR)
rows.Experimental system: Primary brain neuronal cultures from 1–3-day-old human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice on an α-synuclein-knockout background, with 2–3 pups pooled per preparation and FUDR used to inhibit glial proliferation; LRP1-targeting AAV9 guide RNA and Cas9 introduced on culture day 3 overnight, compared with corresponding genotype controls; receptor/Rab5 double immunofluorescence, confocal microscopy, and M1 colocalization analysis in positively transduced neurons. CRISPR methods specify collection after 10 days, whereas general culture methods state experiments were performed on day 21. ARF6 activity and receptor recycling kinetics were not measured.

rows.Finding description: Double staining and confocal M1 analysis of APOE3 versus APOE4 primary mouse neurons found lower LRP1 colocalization with early endosomes, late endosomes (46.7% decrease; Results p < 0.01 versus legend p < 0.001) and lysosomes (20.2% decrease, p < 0.05), but no significant difference with recycling endosomes, using 25–37 cells per receptor–compartment comparison from 2–3 preparations, although the Fig 8A legend describes lysosomal colocalization as unchanged.
rows.Finding quote: The first pattern which was observed with LRP1, shows that lower levels of colocalization of this receptor in the early endosomes in APOE4 neurons (seen also in Fig. 5) was accompanied by lower levels of their colocalization with late endosomes (46.7% decrease, p < 0.01) and lysosomes (20.2% decrease, p < 0.05), while no difference between the genotypes was seen in the corresponding recycling endosomes.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower LRP1 colocalization with early endosomes, late endosomes and lysosomes; no change in LRP1 colocalization with recycling endosomes)
rows.Experimental system: Primary brain-derived, neuron-enriched cultures from 1–3-day-old human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mouse pups on an α-syn-/- background; 2–3 pups pooled per culture, FUDR treatment on culture day 3 to inhibit glial proliferation, experiments on culture day 21; double immunofluorescent staining of LRP1 with Rab5, Rab7, CatD or Rab11, confocal microscopy and M1 colocalization analysis of morphologically selected neurons.

rows.Finding description: Double-label immunofluorescence and confocal microscopy showed significantly greater APOER2 colocalization with Rab5-positive early endosomes in APOE4 primary mouse neurons (M1 = 0.50±0.03, 31 neurons) than APOE3 neurons (M1 = 0.37±0.04, 20 neurons), with three preparations per genotype. Effect is the ratio of the two group values printed in the quote (0.50±0.03 and 0.37±0.04).
rows.Finding quote: Similar analysis of the effect of the APOE genotype on the colocalization of APOER2 with the early endosomes revealed an opposite effect to that seen with LRP1; Accordingly, more APOER2 is localized in the early endosomes in APOE4 cells as indicated by the M1 colocalization variable described in the material and methods section (0.50±0.03, N = 31 from 3 different preparations) than in the APOE3 cells (0.37±0.04, N = 20 from 3 different preparations) neurons (p < 0.05).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (greater APOER2 colocalization with Rab5-positive early endosomes in primary mouse neurons)
rows.Experimental system: Primary brain neuronal cultures from 1–3-day-old APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mouse pups on an α-synuclein-knockout background; each culture pooled 2–3 pups, with FUDR treatment on culture day 3 to inhibit glial proliferation; assayed on culture day 21 using APOER2/Rab5 double immunofluorescence, confocal microscopy, and M1 colocalization analysis of morphologically selected neurons.

rows.Finding description: Double immunofluorescence showed significantly greater insulin receptor colocalization with early endosomes in APOE4 primary mouse neurons (M1 = 0.36±0.02; 34 neurons) than APOE3 neurons (M1 = 0.28±0.02; 48 neurons), with each genotype sampled from four different preparations.
rows.Finding quote: Quantification of these results revealed that the colocalization of IR with early endosomes was significantly higher in APOE4 neurons (0.36±0.02, N = 34 from 4 different preparations) than in the APOE3 neurons (0.28±0.02, N = 48, from 4 different preparations, p < 0.05), as was the colocalization of VEGFR with early endosomes which was higher in APOE4 neurons (0.39±0.03, N = 19 from 2 different preparations) than and in APOE3 neurons (0.24±0.02, N = 20, from 2 different preparations, p < 0.01).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (greater insulin receptor colocalization with early endosomes in primary mouse neurons)
rows.Experimental system: Primary brain-derived neurons from 1–3-day-old human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mouse pups on an α-syn-/- background; cultures pooled 2–3 pups, received FUDR on day 3 to inhibit glial proliferation, and were assayed on culture day 21 without an additional experimental treatment; double immunofluorescence for IR and Rab5, confocal microscopy, and M1 colocalization analysis. Endosomal localization served as a surrogate for trafficking; ARF6 involvement and recycling kinetics were not measured.

rows.Finding description: Double immunofluorescence and confocal microscopy showed greater VEGFR colocalization with Rab5-positive early endosomes in APOE4 primary mouse neurons (M1: 0.39±0.03; 19 neurons) than APOE3 neurons (M1: 0.24±0.02; 20 neurons), with two independent preparations per genotype.
rows.Finding quote: Quantification of these results revealed that the colocalization of IR with early endosomes was significantly higher in APOE4 neurons (0.36±0.02, N = 34 from 4 different preparations) than in the APOE3 neurons (0.28±0.02, N = 48, from 4 different preparations, p < 0.05), as was the colocalization of VEGFR with early endosomes which was higher in APOE4 neurons (0.39±0.03, N = 19 from 2 different preparations) than and in APOE3 neurons (0.24±0.02, N = 20, from 2 different preparations, p < 0.01).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (greater VEGFR colocalization with early endosomes in primary mouse neurons)
rows.Experimental system: Primary brain neuronal-enriched cultures from 1–3-day-old APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mouse pups on an α-syn-/- background; 2–3 pups pooled per culture, FUDR treatment on culture day 3 to inhibit glial proliferation, and experiments on day 21; VEGFR2/Rab5 double immunofluorescence, confocal microscopy, and M1 colocalization analysis of morphologically selected neurons. ARF6 and recycling kinetics were not measured.

rows.Finding description: Double-staining confocal microscopy of primary mouse neurons showed that APOE4 versus APOE3 increased VEGFR colocalization with early endosomes and decreased colocalization with late endosomes by 47.74%, lysosomes by 31.30%, and recycling endosomes by 29.02% (25–37 cells per receptor–compartment analysis).
rows.Finding quote: Additionally, there was also a decrease in the colocalization of the receptors with the lysosomes in APOE4 neurons that was significant in APOER2 and VEGFR but not in the IR (APOER2 : 35.89% decrease, p < 0.0001; VEGFR: 31.30% decrease, p < 0.05), and in the recycling endosomes in all three receptors (APOER2 : 11.16% decrease, p = 0.5154; IR: 30.88% decrease, p < 0.05; VEGFR: 29.02% decrease, p < 0.05) when compared to APOE3 neurons.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (increased VEGFR colocalization with early endosomes; decreased VEGFR colocalization with late endosomes, lysosomes, and recycling endosomes)
rows.Experimental system: Primary brain-derived neuronal-enriched cultures from 1–3-day-old human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mouse pups on an α-synuclein-knockout background; 2–3 pups pooled per culture, FUDR applied on culture day 3 to inhibit glial proliferation, and experiments performed on day 21; VEGFR2 double immunostaining with Rab5, Rab7, CatD, or Rab11, followed by confocal microscopy and M1 colocalization analysis of morphologically selected neurons; 2–3 different preparations. ARF6 activity and receptor recycling kinetics were not measured.

rows.Finding description: Double immunostaining and confocal microscopy showed significantly lower LRP1 colocalization with Rab5-positive early endosomes in APOE4 primary mouse neurons (M1 = 0.11±0.016; 27 neurons) than APOE3 neurons (M1 = 0.24±0.02; 21 neurons), with each genotype sampled from two preparations. Effect is the ratio of the two group values printed in the quote (0.24±0.02 and 0.11±0.016).
rows.Finding quote: Evaluation of the extent of colocalization of the ApoE receptors with the early endosomes (marked in yellow pixels in Fig. 5) revealed that there is a greater localization of LRP1 in early endosomes in APOE3 neurons (0.24±0.02, N = 21 from 2 different preparations) compared to APOE4 (0.11±0.016, N = 27 from 2 different preparations). This difference between the APOE4 and the APOE3 cells is highly significant (p < 0.001).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower LRP1 colocalization with early endosomes in primary mouse neurons)
rows.Experimental system: Primary neuron-enriched brain cultures from 1–3-day-old human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mouse pups on an α-synuclein-null background; 2–3 pups pooled per culture; FUDR treatment on day 3 to inhibit glial proliferation; assayed on culture day 21 by LRP1/Rab5 double immunofluorescence, confocal microscopy, and M1 colocalization analysis.

rows.Finding description: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated APOER2 knockdown reduced early-endosomal colocalization of IR by 55.1% and VEGFR by 52.6% in APOE4 primary mouse neurons, with no significant difference in either receptor’s colocalization in APOE3 neurons or in LRP1 localization; measurements included 34–38 neurons for IR and 24–28 neurons for VEGFR, each from three preparations.
rows.Finding quote: A different pattern was observed with the growth factor receptors IR and VEGFR, where knocking down APOER2 increased the levels of IR (50.9% increase relative to APOE4 control) and VEGFR (21.3% increase relative to APOE4 control) in APOE4 neurons and decreased their colocalization with early endosomes (IR: 55.1% reduction, and VEGFR: 52.6% reduction relative to APOE4 control). In contrast, both the levels and the colocalization of IR and VEGFR in APOE3 neurons were not affected by APOER2 knock down.
rows.Finding summary: (APOER2 knockdown in APOE4 primary mouse neurons) -> (lower IR and VEGFR early-endosomal colocalization); (APOR2 knockdown in APOE3 neurons) -> (no change in IR or VEGFR early-endosomal colocalization); (APOER2 knockdown) -> (no change in LRP1 early-endosomal colocalization)
rows.Experimental system: Primary brain-derived neuronal-enriched cultures from 1–3-day-old APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mouse pups on an α-syn-/- background, pooling 2–3 pups per culture. APOER2-targeting AAV9 guide RNAs and Cas9 were introduced on culture day 3 overnight; medium was replaced the following day and cells collected for immunofluorescence 10 days later according to the CRISPR/Cas9 methods. Positively transfected neurons were analyzed by receptor/Rab5 double immunostaining, confocal microscopy and M1 colocalization analysis. ARF6 activity and recycling kinetics were not measured.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, for example astrocytes, APOE4 causes impaired ARF6-related recycling of receptors between the cell surface and the endosome, compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Surface biotinylation measurements in Reelin-stimulated primary mouse cortical neurons showed lower cell-surface GluA1, GluA2/3, and GluN2B levels with human ApoE4 than with ApoE3.
rows.Finding quote: The powerful effect of ApoE4 on NMDA receptor function correlated with the almost complete suppression of Reelin-dependent GluN2 subunit tyrosine phosphorylation ( Fig. 2 G ) and a reduction of not only NMDA but also AMPA receptor subunits at the cell surface ( Fig. 2 H and I ), consistent with the absence of an isoform effect on AMPA/NMDA ratios ( Fig. S1 and Tables S1 – S4 ).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower cell-surface GluA1, GluA2/3, and GluN2B in Reelin-stimulated primary mouse cortical neurons)
rows.Experimental system: Primary cortical neurons from embryonic day 18 wild-type mice, cultured for 12–13 days in vitro; treated with human ApoE3 or ApoE4 lipoproteins naturally secreted by stably transfected HEK293 cells, at 3 μg/mL with Reelin for 15 min at 37 °C according to the supplementary surface-biotinylation protocol. Surface proteins were labeled with membrane-impermeable sulfo-NHS-SS-biotin, captured with NeutrAvidin, and immunoblotted for GluA1, GluA2/3, and GluN2B. Mouse strain and panel-specific Reelin concentration were not stated; ARF6 was not measured.

rows.Finding description: In four independent experiments, primary mouse cortical neurons treated with ApoE4 (3 μg/mL, 15 minutes) had lower surface Apoer2 normalized to total Apoer2 than neurons treated with ApoE3, ApoE2, or control, measured by biotinylation and immunoblotting, with significance reported versus control.
rows.Finding quote: Whereas ApoE2 (lane 2) and ApoE3 (lane 3) did not reduce surface expression of Apoer2 compared with the control (lane 1), ApoE4 significantly decreased surface expression of this “dual function” Reelin and ApoE receptor (lane 4), suggesting that Apoer2 availability, and thus function, at the cell surface might be impaired.
rows.Finding summary: (ApoE3 -> ApoE4) -> (lower surface Apoer2 normalized to total Apoer2 in primary mouse cortical neurons)
rows.Experimental system: Primary cortical neurons from embryonic day 18 wild-type mice, cultured for 12–13 days in vitro; treated without added Reelin with naturally secreted human ApoE2, ApoE3, or ApoE4 from stably transfected HEK293 cells at 3 μg/mL for 15 minutes at 37 °C, or control conditioned medium; membrane-impermeable surface biotinylation, NeutrAvidin capture, and Apoer2 immunoblotting, normalized to total cellular Apoer2 and standardized to control.

rows.Finding description: Primary mouse cortical neurons incubated with Reelin and human ApoE isoforms for 2 hours had substantially lower surface Apoer2 with ApoE4 than with ApoE3 or ApoE2.
rows.Finding quote: All ApoE isoforms ( Fig. 1 C , lanes 2–4) significantly decreased surface expression of Apoer2 upon Reelin stimulation compared with control (lane 1). ApoE3 was marginally, but not significantly, more effective than ApoE2, whereas ApoE4 led to a dramatic and statistically highly significant reduction of Apoer2 at the neuronal cell surface.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower surface Apoer2 in Reelin-stimulated primary mouse cortical neurons)
rows.Experimental system: Primary cortical neurons from wild-type mouse E18 embryos, cultured for 12–13 days in vitro; treated with HEK293-secreted human ApoE isoforms at 3 μg/mL together with Reelin at 2 μg/mL for 2 hours at 37 °C, as specified in Fig. 1C. Surface Apoer2 was measured by membrane-impermeable biotinylation, neutravidin capture and immunoblotting, normalized to total cellular Apoer2; mouse strain was not specified.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 adheres more tightly to some recycling receptors than APOE3, impeding recycling.

rows.Finding description: ApoE4 increased colocalization of sortilin–FABP7 proximity-ligation signals with Rab11-positive recycling endosomes relative to apoE3, measured in 38 cells per condition.
rows.Finding quote: Altered sorting of sortilin–FABP7 complexes in the presence of apoE4 was confirmed quantitatively by colocalization studies documenting trapping of PLA signals for sortilin and FABP7 in early endosomes (marked by Rab5; Fig. 7F,H) and recycling endosomes (marked by Rab11; Fig. 7G,I) in the presence of apoE4 as compared with apoE3.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (greater recycling-endosomal colocalization of sortilin–FABP7 complexes)
rows.Experimental system: CHO-K1-derived Chinese hamster ovary cells stably overexpressing mouse sortilin and Myc-tagged mouse FABP7 (CHO-S/F), treated for 24 h with HEK293-conditioned medium containing 5 µg/ml human apoE3 or apoE4. Proximity-ligation signals were co-stained for Rab11; blinded single-z-plane analysis used thresholded Manders’ coefficient tM1. The experiment was replicated three times. These are non-neural hamster cells, not human brain cells.

rows.Finding description: Across three independent experiments, apoE4 treatment shifted total sortilin immunostaining toward a perinuclear distribution compared with apoE3.
rows.Finding quote: PLA signals for sortilin–FABP7 complexes change from a dispersed vesicular pattern with apoE3 to a perinuclear pattern with apoE4 (arrowheads). A similar change is seen for total sortilin, whereas the pattern for total FABP7 remains unaffected by apoE4.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (more perinuclear localization of sortilin)
rows.Experimental system: CHO-K1-derived Chinese hamster ovary cells stably overexpressing mouse sortilin and Myc-tagged mouse FABP7 (CHO-S/F), treated for 24 h with HEK293-conditioned medium containing 5 µg/ml human apoE3 or apoE4; sortilin immunostaining and fixed-cell microscopy. These are non-neural hamster cells, not human brain cells.

rows.Finding description: Across three independent experiments, apoE4 treatment shifted sortilin–FABP7 complexes from the dispersed vesicular distribution observed with apoE3 to a confined perinuclear distribution.
rows.Finding quote: As shown in Fig. 7E, the intracellular distribution of sortilin–FABP7 complexes (as detected through a PLA) changed from a dispersed vesicular pattern with apoE3 to a confined perinuclear appearance with apoE4.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (more confined perinuclear localization of sortilin–FABP7 complexes)
rows.Experimental system: CHO-K1-derived Chinese hamster ovary cells stably overexpressing mouse sortilin and Myc-tagged mouse FABP7 (CHO-S/F), treated for 24 h with HEK293-conditioned medium containing 5 µg/ml human apoE3 or apoE4; fixed-cell proximity ligation assay and microscopy. These are non-neural hamster cells, not human brain cells.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 adheres more tightly to some recycling receptors than APOE3, impeding recycling.

rows.Finding description: Fig. 3A includes cells without heparinase. The authors report 1.3-fold higher binding for apoE3 than apoE4, a nonsignificant difference, without assigning that ratio separately to the untreated arm.
rows.Finding quote: The binding ability of apoE3-F-EP was 1.3-fold higher than that of apoE4-F-EP; however, the difference was not statistically signiﬁcant.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (no significant change in LRP1-associated cell-surface particle binding)
rows.Experimental system: Human GM00701 fibroblasts obtained from Coriell Institute, described as highly expressing LRP1 with little or no LDLR and SDC1; no heparinase pretreatment; synthetic triolein/PC/NBD-PC emulsion particles carrying recombinant human apoE3 or apoE4 at 2.0 mg/dL apoE; incubation for 3 h at 4 °C; whole-cell fluorescence normalized to cellular protein. These were peripheral fibroblasts, not brain cells; receptor recycling and binding kinetics were not measured.
rows.Data location: Fig. 3A, apoE3 versus apoE4 across the binding experiments

rows.Finding description: Fluorescence microscopy reproduced the reported isoform-dependent binding pattern, with apoE4 below apoE3, but an apoE4-versus-apoE3 microscopy-specific effect size or significance was not stated.
rows.Finding quote: These differences among apoE isoforms were also observed under a ﬂuorescence microscope (Fig. 3B).
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (qualitatively lower cell-associated particle fluorescence)
rows.Experimental system: Human Coriell GM00701 fibroblasts incubated with recombinant human apoE-containing synthetic fluorescent emulsion particles at 2.0 mg/dL apoE for 3 h at 4 °C; fluorescence microscopy at 100× magnification and ImageJ quantification. The legend describes representative images from three independent experiments and relative fluorescence calculated from 30 cells; receptor recycling was not measured.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 adheres more tightly to some recycling receptors than APOE3, impeding recycling.

rows.Finding description: In quadruplicate J774 macrophage binding assays, recombinant apoE3- and apoE4-enriched VLDL both efficiently competed with radiolabelled LDL for receptor binding; no significant difference between apoE4 and apoE3 was reported, although no statistical comparison was provided.
rows.Finding quote: Each VLDL particle competed efficiently (fig. 4), except for the recombinant apolipoprotein E2 complex and apolipoprotein E deficient VLDL, as ex- pected.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (no change in reported ability of apoE-enriched VLDL to compete for LDL receptor binding)
rows.Experimental system: Mouse J774 macrophage cell line; human recombinant apoE3 and apoE4 expressed in E. coli BL21(DE3) as fusion proteins with a 42-amino-acid amino-terminal extension. ApoE-deficient VLDL isolated from apoE-knockout mice were separately enriched with each isoform for 1 hour at 37 °C and separated from free apoE by ultracentrifugation. Following 20 hours in medium containing lipid-free human serum, macrophages underwent quadruplicate competition incubations with 125I-labelled LDL and unlabelled competitors for 3 hours on melting ice. Cell-associated radioactivity measured LDL binding. Recombinant apoE loading differed between the VLDL preparations; receptor recycling was not measured.
rows.Data location: Fig. 4; Results, LDL receptor binding studies
